label: Constructing Symplectic Manifolds
notes: This chapter, spanning printed pages 289 through 340, leaves classification behind and asks how new symplectic manifolds are built from old ones. Four moves organize the story: blowing up and down, connected and fiber sums, the telescope or cutting construction, and Donaldson hypersurfaces that supply symplectic submanifolds in any class.

label: Why Build, Not Classify
notes: Symplectic manifolds resist Riemannian-style classification, so progress comes from a toolkit of cut-and-paste surgeries. Each operation must preserve closedness and nondegeneracy of the form while changing topology in a controlled way. Tracking what each construction preserves, and what it costs in area or homology, is the unifying theme of the chapter.

label: The Symplectic Blow-Up
notes: Blowing up a point removes a small open ball and replaces its boundary sphere by an exceptional divisor, a copy of complex projective space whose lines are collapsed to points. The construction depends on a size parameter equal to the radius of the excised ball, which fixes the symplectic area of the exceptional class.

label: Local Model of the Blow-Up
notes: The tautological line bundle over projective space carries a fibrewise form that, away from the zero section, matches the standard form on the punctured ball. Gluing this model into the manifold realizes the blow-up symplectically. The exceptional divisor receives area proportional to the chosen size, and away from it nothing changes.

label: Blow-Down and the Size Parameter
notes: Blow-down reverses the surgery: an exceptional sphere of the right area is collapsed back to a point, restoring a ball. The size parameter is the bookkeeping device. In dimension four the exceptional class has self-intersection negative one, and its area must equal the parameter for the inverse construction to be symplectic.

label: Moment Polytope Picture
notes: For toric manifolds the blow-up is visible as a corner chop of the moment polytope. Slicing a triangle of side epsilon off a vertex introduces a new edge, the image of the exceptional divisor, whose length records the blow-up size. The lost Liouville area equals one half the square of the clipping size.

label: Connected Sums of Manifolds
notes: An ordinary smooth connected sum removes a ball from each manifold and glues along the resulting spheres, but this generically destroys a symplectic form because spheres bound. Symplectic topology therefore replaces point surgery with surgery along codimension-two symplectic submanifolds, where normal data can be matched compatibly.

label: The Symplectic Fiber Sum
notes: Gompf's fiber sum glues two symplectic manifolds along symplectomorphic codimension-two submanifolds whose normal bundles are opposite in Euler number. Cutting out tubular neighborhoods and identifying the boundary fibrations by an orientation-reversing bundle map produces a closed symplectic manifold whose form restricts correctly on each piece.

label: Normal Bundles Must Match
notes: The fiber sum succeeds only when the normal bundles of the two copies of the gluing submanifold are inverse, so their Euler numbers sum to zero. This balance lets the symplectic neighborhood theorem provide standard collars that the gluing diffeomorphism can identify while keeping the patched form closed and nondegenerate throughout.

label: The Telescope and Symplectic Cut
notes: The telescope construction, dual to gluing, cuts a manifold along a level set of a circle action and caps each side with a collapsed boundary. Lerman's symplectic cut produces two closed symplectic manifolds from one with a Hamiltonian circle action, and reversing it recovers the symplectic sum along the shared reduced space.

label: Donaldson Submanifolds
notes: Donaldson's theorem produces symplectic hypersurfaces Poincare dual to large multiples of an integral symplectic class. Approximately holomorphic sections of high tensor powers of a line bundle have zero sets that are symplectic submanifolds. This supplies the codimension-two pieces that fiber sums and blow-ups consume as raw material.

label: Lefschetz Pencils
notes: Pushing Donaldson's method to pairs of sections yields Lefschetz pencils: a base locus together with a family of symplectic hypersurfaces having only nondegenerate critical points. Blowing up the base locus turns the pencil into a Lefschetz fibration over the sphere, giving a topological description of symplectic four-manifolds up to the construction.

label: Construction Dependency Map
notes: The four operations interlock: Donaldson hypersurfaces feed fiber sums and blow-ups, the symplectic cut inverts the sum, and pencils package everything into fibrations. Keeping the dependency graph explicit prevents conflating distinct surgeries and clarifies which invariant, area, Euler number, or homology class, each move controls and reports.
